**Form and association**
Michigan High School Athletic Association membership resolution for 2025-26, presented as item 6E on the June 17, 2025 Troy Board of Education agenda. The MHSAA is located at 1661 Ramblewood Drive, East Lansing, MI 48823, telephone (517) 332-5046. It is described as a voluntary, nonprofit corporation of public, private and parochial junior high/middle and senior high schools whose boards of education or governing bodies have applied for and received membership on behalf of their secondary schools. Completed forms are to be saved and sent to camala@mhsaa.com as an attachment, with one signed copy returned and one retained.

**Terms of membership**
The association sponsors statewide tournaments and makes eligibility rules for participation. Boards that wish to host or participate must join and agree to abide by and enforce MHSAA rules, regulations and qualifications on eligibility, game rules and tournament policies, procedures and schedules. Participation in MHSAA postseason tournaments is conditioned on high schools adhering to at least the minimum standards of Regulation I and the maximum limitations of Regulation II in all MHSAA tournament sports. MHSAA tournaments are the collective property of the association rather than of any individual member school, and the association reserves rights over publication information, exclusive arrangements for recognition and exposure, restrictive policies against exploitation and commercialization, proprietary interests, and the use of images or transmissions identifying officials, spectators, students, personnel and marks. Resolutions that are modified or supplemented with letters imposing additional conditions are rejected.

**Resolution language**
The resolution covers the year August 1, 2025 through July 31, 2026 and enrolls the named schools as members of the Michigan High School Athletic Association, Inc. and to participate in its approved interschool athletic activities. The board delegates supervision and control of those activities to the Superintendent or designee, accepts the association's Constitution and By-Laws, and adopts the rules, regulations and interpretations in the current Handbook as minimum standards and as the governing code, agreeing to primary enforcement. The authorization is effective from August 1, 2025 until July 31, 2026 and may not be revoked during that period. A Record of Adoption block provides for the day and month in 2025, the governing body name, board secretary or designee signature, address, city and zip, and contact e-mail; all are blank.

**Eligibility rules for listed schools**
Under the MHSAA Constitution, high schools, junior high/middle schools and comparable schools may join provided the building has enrollment and onsite attendance of at least 15 students, whether grades 6 through 8 or 9, 7 through 8 or 9, or 9 or 10 through 12, and provided nonpublic schools qualify for federal income tax exemption as not-for-profit organizations. Schools may join at the 6th-grade level to reach the 15-student minimum whether or not 6th-graders participate. Districts are not required to hold junior high/middle school membership or to sponsor 6th-grade athletics. If a listed junior high/middle school sponsors a 6th-grade team in any sport or lets a 6th-grader play with 7th and 8th graders, all of Regulations III and IV apply to all 6th-graders in all sports involving 6th-graders on that school's teams; if no 6th-graders participate in a sport, MHSAA rules do not apply in that sport.

**Completed entry**
The school listing pages are largely blank templates for up to 15 high schools and multiple junior high/middle schools. The single filled entry is line 4 under member junior high/middle schools: SMITH MIDDLE SCHOOL, grade configuration 6-8, anticipated 2025-26 7th and 8th grade enrollment of 419, anticipated 2025-26 6th-grade enrollment of 184, with Yes marked for 6th-graders participating in at least one sport with 7th and 8th graders and grade levels for membership marked 6, 7 and 8.
https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.verbose:
The Michigan High School Athletic Association 2025-26 membership resolution form appears as agenda item 6E for the Troy School District Board of Education meeting of June 17, 2025. The association's address is 1661 Ramblewood Drive, East Lansing, MI 48823, with telephone (517) 332-5046. The MHSAA is described as a voluntary, nonprofit corporation comprised of public, private and parochial junior high/middle and senior high schools whose boards of education or governing bodies have voluntarily applied for and received membership for and on behalf of their secondary schools. The association sponsors statewide tournaments and makes eligibility rules with respect to participation in MHSAA-sponsored tournaments in the various sports. Each board of education or governing body that wishes to host or participate in such meets and tournaments must join the MHSAA and agree to abide by and enforce MHSAA rules, regulations and qualifications concerning eligibility, game rules, and tournament policies, procedures and schedules. It is stated as a condition for participation in any MHSAA postseason tournaments that high schools adhere to at least the minimum standards of Regulation I and the maximum limitations of Regulation II in all MHSAA tournament sports.

The form asserts that MHSAA tournaments are the collective property of the MHSAA and not of any individual member school, and that the association reserves the right to promote and advance the membership's interests through publication information; exclusive arrangements to create recognition and exposure for school-sponsored activities; restrictive policies prohibiting exploitation and commercialization of MHSAA-sponsored tournaments; appropriate proprietary interests; and the use of images or transmissions identifying contest officials, spectators, and member schools' students, personnel and marks. To obtain membership the board of education or governing body must adopt the resolution for its junior high/middle and senior high schools; the resolution must be formally ratified and properly signed, with one signed copy returned to the MHSAA for its files and one copy retained. Resolutions that are modified in any way or supplemented with letters placing additional conditions on MHSAA membership or tournament participation are to be rejected. The form directs the user twice to save the document and send it to camala@mhsaa.com as an attachment.

The membership resolution itself is captioned for the year August 1, 2025 through July 31, 2026. It provides blanks for the schools under the direction of the board, the city or township, and the county, all within the State of Michigan, and states that such schools are hereby (A) enrolled as members of the Michigan High School Athletic Association, Inc., a nonprofit association, and (B) further enrolled to participate in the approved interschool athletic activities sponsored by that association. The board of education or governing body delegates to the Superintendent or designee the responsibility for the supervision and control of those activities, accepts the Constitution and By-Laws of the association, and adopts as its own the rules, regulations and interpretations, as minimum standards, published in the current Handbook as the governing code under which the schools shall conduct their program of interscholastic athletics, agreeing to primary enforcement of those rules, regulations, interpretations and qualifications. Schools that host or participate in association meets and tournaments must follow and enforce all tournament policies, procedures and schedules. The authorization is effective from August 1, 2025 and remains effective until July 31, 2026, during which period it may not be revoked. A note specifies that junior high/middle and senior high schools of the school system to be listed as MHSAA members and to receive MHSAA mailings during 2025-26 must be listed on the back of the form.

The Record of Adoption block states that the resolution was adopted by the board of education or governing body of named schools on a blank day of a blank month, 2025, and is so recorded in the minutes of that board's meeting. Signature lines are provided for the governing body name, board secretary signature or designee with a checkbox to indicate a designee, address, city and zip code, and contact e-mail. As presented, these lines are unfilled.

The reverse side, headed Schools Which Are To Be MHSAA Members During 2025-26, sets out eligibility conditions from the MHSAA Constitution. All high schools, junior high/middle schools, or other Michigan schools doing a corresponding grade of work may become members provided that the school building has enrollment and onsite attendance of at least 15 students, whether for grades 6 through 8 or 9, grades 7 through 8 or 9, or grades 9 or 10 through 12; and, if a nonpublic school, that the school qualifies for federal income tax exemption as a not-for-profit organization. To reach the 15-student minimum for middle school membership, schools may join the MHSAA at the 6th-grade level whether or not 6th-grade students participate in athletics. Paragraph A states that the section does not require school districts to become member schools at the junior high/middle school level and does not require districts to sponsor any interscholastic athletics for 6th-grade students. Paragraph B states that if a district's MHSAA Membership Resolution lists a junior high/middle school as a member school, and if that school sponsors a 6th-grade team in any sport or permits a 6th-grade student to participate with 7th- and/or 8th-grade students in any sport, then all of Regulations III and IV apply to all 6th-graders in all sports involving 6th-graders on teams sponsored by that school; if the school does not allow any 6th-graders to participate in a sport, MHSAA rules do not apply in that sport.

The listing pages provide numbered blanks for up to fifteen member high schools and separate blocks for member junior high/middle schools covering 6th, 7th and 8th-grade buildings, each block asking for the name of the member school, the configuration of grades in the building with examples K-6, 6-8, 7-8 and 7-9, anticipated 2025-26 7th and 8th-grade enrollment, anticipated 2025-26 6th-grade enrollment, grade levels for membership among 6, 7 and 8, and a yes/no indication of whether 6th-graders will participate in at least one sport with 7th and 8th graders, with a line for the building housing 6th-graders if not the same building. Instructions direct that junior high/middle schools be listed separately from high schools even where all grades are housed in the same building, and that additional schools be listed on a separate sheet if necessary.

Only one school entry is completed in the document as presented. Under member junior high/middle schools, line 4 names SMITH MIDDLE SCHOOL, with the configuration of grades in the building given as 6-8, the anticipated 2025-26 7th and 8th-grade enrollment given as 419, and the anticipated 2025-26 6th-grade enrollment given as 184. The Yes box is marked X for 6th-graders participating in at least one sport with 7th and 8th graders, with the line for a separate building housing 6th-graders left blank, and grade levels for membership are marked X for 6, X for 7 and X for 8.
